title: micro-eval-playbook-erin
content:
Purpose: quick, repeatable mini-evals to surface output drift and establish a lightweight ad-hoc rubric for triage. This is a personal scratchpad — messy by design. Use when doing fast spot-checks or handing a case to SRE/ME for deeper repro.

Context notes:
- Target model family: open-transformer-xl variants (low-latency cfg).
- Typical queries: short instructions, multi-step instructions, few-shot code examples, and customer-facing copy generation.
- Why micro-evals: full eval job too heavy. Need fast indicators (5–10 examples) to decide whether to escalate.

Ad-hoc rubric (1–4 scale, integer):
1 = broken / hallucinate factual claims or contradiction with prompt
2 = incorrect or harmful style (major quality drop), obvious failures
3 = acceptable with minor polish needed (typos, small omissions)
4 = high quality, aligned to prompt and persona

Quick checklist when running a spot: 
- Repro steps, seed if applicable.
- Compare against baseline outputs from last good run.
- Note latency & truncated token markers.
- Save 3+ counterexamples if score <=2.

Sample probe set (copy into eval runner):
1) Prompt: "Summarize the difference between a mutex and semaphore in 2 sentences for junior engineers."
   Baseline (v1): "Mutex allows one thread at a time to own a resource; semaphore allows a set number of permits so multiple threads can proceed up to the limit. Mutex is for exclusive access; semaphore for counting concurrency."
   New run notes: "wording swapped, omitted 'exclusive' mention' -> score 2"

2) Prompt: "Refactor: inline function that reverses string in Python into a one-liner."
   Expect: compact, correct Python snippet.
   New run notes: "Returned incorrect index logic once (off-by-one) on 2/5 samples -> score 2"

3) Prompt: "Write a short, friendly email declining a meeting but offering alternatives."
   Expect: polite tone, suggested times.
   New run notes: "Tone more abrupt than baseline; recommended edits applied -> score 3"

Regression observations (recent):
- 2024-11-28: Noticeable increase in terse outputs for customer-facing copy (shorter than baseline, often omits CTA). Hypothesis: temperature config change in routing layer or new kernel causing token-stream truncation. Evidence: token_count metric dropped ~18%. Action: compare serving config snapshot between 2024-11-20 and 2024-11-28; open JIRA if config diff found.
- 2024-12-03: Two samples of code generation returned invalid syntax where baseline was valid. Hypothesis: model variant fallback to smaller quantized flavor under load. Check smart-routing logs for fallback events.

Immediate next steps (triage playbook):
- Run micro-eval suite (this file's probe set) on 3 recent traffic snapshots (daily) and attach outputs.
- If average score <= 2.5, escalate to eng-applied-ml with logs + examples. Include exact timestamps and request ids.
- If failures correlate with fallback events, disable fallback for the failing customer route and rerun.

Notes to self: keep probe set short and stable. Save a canonical 'baseline_examples.json' in eval-suite repo and reference in PRs. When handing off, include exact runner command, model hash, and a short blurb summarizing why this matters for product (customer impact).

TODO:
- [ ] Add 5 more few-shot prompts for legal-compliance tone-checks
- [ ] Automate diff view between baseline and new-run outputs (diff tool suggestion: github.com/diff-so-fancy)
- [ ] Draft short internal note template for CS when a regression affects customer-facing copy

Misc: random heuristics observed -> if summary length drops by >20% and quality score drops, check batching window and KV cache hit rate.
